scenes.narration: Text in Python is called a string. You put it inside quotes, single or double, as long as both ends match. Think of a string of beads. Each character is one bead. scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: adding a string and a number
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We try to add text and a number. Python says, type error. It can only concatenate a string, not an int, to a string. Plus joins text to text, or adds number to number. It does not guess. Give print both values with a comma instead, and Python handles the rest.

shorts.title: What is a string?
shorts.hook: "Text in Python is called a string."
shorts.script: Text in Python is called a string. You put it inside quotes, single or double, and both ends must match. Hello is a string. A name is a string. Even a number inside quotes is a string, and not a number any more. Think of a string of beads, where every character is one bead. That is why we call it a string. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Strings in 40 seconds.

shorts.title: Count with len
shorts.hook: "The len function counts the characters in a string."
shorts.script: The len function counts the characters in a string. Len of Xecxec is six, one for each letter. Spaces count too, and so do commas and apostrophes. So len of the text with the apostrophe is eight. Use len when you need to know how long a word is. Say the characters out loud as you count. Then you do not miscount. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Counting characters.

shorts.title: Join and repeat
shorts.script: Two string tricks. A plus sign joins two strings into one longer string, so Hello comma space plus Xecxec makes Hello, Xecxec. A star repeats a string, so ha times three makes ha ha ha with no spaces. Joining and repeating never change the old strings. They make brand new ones every single time. Try both in your own file and see. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Plus joins, star repeats.

shorts.title: String plus number
shorts.script: Very common bug. You write text plus a number, and Python says type error. It can only concatenate a string, not an int, to a string. Plus joins text to text, or adds number to number. It does not guess. The easy fix is to give print both values with a comma. Then print does the joining for you. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Plus will not guess.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: "Why did the string go to the beach?"
shorts.script: Why did the string go to the beach? It wanted to catch some waves in its quotes. Now your challenge. Make two names, first and last. Print them joined with a space between them. Then print the first name three times in a row. Use plus for the joining and star for the repeating. Share your answer in the comments. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 07.
